texts.preamble: Dilip Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 December, 2025 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:31096 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 1 st Of December, 2025 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 6 of 2024 Dilip Kumar Gupta Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Appearance: Shri Deependra Singh Raghuwanshi, Advocate for the ap Shri G.K. Agrawal, Govt. Advocate for respondent/Stat Order
texts.facts: Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 22/3/2021, Food Safety Officer collected samples of Namkeen which was being manufactured by the appellant. In the complaint, it is mentioned that the manufacturing was being done in a most unhygienic manner and on a dirty floor. It was informed by the appellant that the Namkeen is meant for sale. as per law and, accordingly, they were sent to the Laboratory. The Food Analyst, as per his report (Ex.P/25), found that Namkeen Jain Special Namkeen (Pack) was misbranded, Palmolein Oil Ref. palmolein oil (loose) was found to be substandard vide report (Ex.P/26) and Wheat flour wheat flour was also found to be misbranded as per report (Ex.P/30), whereas Besan was found within norms. Accordingly notice was given to the Dilip Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187346620/ 1 appellant and an option was also given that if he is not satisfied with the report of the Food Analyst, then he can prefer an appeal under section 46 of FSSA. The appellant did not prefer an appeal and accordingly complaint was filed. Being aggrieved by the said order, appellant preferred an appeal which too has been dismissed by the impugned order passed by the IX District Judge Gwalior/ appellate Authority. 4. Challenging the orders passed by the Court below/Adjudicating Officer, a solitary ground was raised by counsel for appellant that the penalty imposed by the Authorities is on a higher side and, therefore, it may be reduced. From the complaint, it is clear that at the time of inspection it was found that the Namkeen was being prepared in a most unhygienic manner and the raw material was lying on the dirty floor. The inspection note (Ex.P/14) was prepared and it has been mentioned as under:- "..... (unhygienic and unhealthy) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31096 3 MSA-6-2024 , , , , ....." 7. Thus it is clear that not only the palmolein oil was found to be substandard but even Jain special Namkeen and wheat flour were found to be misbranded. Under these circumstances, penalty of Rs. 50,000/- for violation of section 51, Rs. 20,000/- for violation of section 52, Rs. 10,000/- for violation of section 56 and Rs. 20,000/- for violation of section 58 cannot be said to be on higher side.
